declarations.description:
A dropdown built from a trigger button and a `c2-list` of `c2-list-item` rows inside a `c2-overlay` popover. The
rows are the light-DOM children of the select, so they are themed with the `--c2-list-item--*` variables directly on
the select (or on a wrapper); the dropdown container is themed through the `--c2-select__list--*` variables and the
trigger through `--c2-select__button--*`. The select has no intrinsic width: give the host a `width` (or place it in
a grid/flex cell) and the trigger fills it.

Keyboard: Enter, Space, ArrowDown or ArrowUp on the trigger opens the dropdown and moves focus to the selected
option (else the first). The list then takes arrows, Home/End and typeahead; Enter or Space picks. Picking (single
select) or Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger; Tab leaves the select and closes the dropdown.

Groups: `<h3>` (any heading level) and `<hr>` among the options are group headings and dividers; the list skips
them for selection and keyboard. They are styled by the `--c2-list__heading--*` and `--c2-list__divider--*`
variables, set on the select.

Search: `searchable` puts a search field above the options. It takes focus when the dropdown opens and hides every
option whose text does not contain what was typed (case and accents ignored), and a group heading with nothing left
under it. ArrowDown moves to the first match, Enter picks it, ArrowUp from the first match returns to the field and
typing on an option goes on in the field. Hidden options are hidden by a style rule in the select's own shadow
root: nothing is written on them. The search runs only while the dropdown is open; closing it clears the text. Each
keystroke fires `search-change`: cancel it to filter yourself (replace the options with a server's answer, setting
`loading` meanwhile). `creatable` adds a "Create" row while no option's text equals the search; it fires
`create-option`, and the app adds the option and selects it. The `footer` slot below the options is the place for
the panel's actions (Clear, Apply), the app's own buttons.

members.name: handleHostActivation
members.description: WebKit associates form labels but does not focus a form-associated custom element when its label activates it.

members.name: setQuery
members.description: Stores the search text and asks the app, through `search-change`, whether the select filters it.

members.name: focusRow
members.description:
Moves focus to an option, and the list's roving tabindex with it: the list would otherwise keep it on an option
the search hid, which Shift+Tab from the footer could not reach.

members.name: visibleRows
members.description: The options the search leaves visible and enabled, in order: where the keyboard may go. `all` keeps the hidden ones.

members.name: handleListKeydown
members.default: { capture: true, handleEvent: (event: KeyboardEvent) => { if (!this.searchable) return const rows = this.visibleRows() const index = rows.indexOf(event.target as ListItem) if (index < 0) return const typing = !event.ctrlKey && !event.metaKey && !event.altKey && (event.key === 'Backspace' || (event.key.length === 1 && event.key !== ' ')) let next: HTMLElement | undefined // The arrows, Home and End are taken whatever the modifiers: the list would move onto a hidden option. if (event.key === 'ArrowDown') next = rows[index + 1] ?? this.createButton ?? rows[index] else if (event.key === 'ArrowUp') next = rows[index - 1] ?? this.searchInput else if (event.key === 'Home') next = rows[0] else if (event.key === 'End') next = rows[rows.length - 1] else if (typing) { next = this.searchInput this.setQuery(event.key === 'Backspace' ? this.query.slice(0, -1) : this.query + event.key) } if (!next) return event.preventDefault() event.stopPropagation() this.focusRow(next) }, }
members.description:
With `searchable`, the keyboard on an option moves among the visible ones only (the list itself would land on a
hidden one), leaves for the search field above the first and the Create row below the last, and sends typing to
the search field. Runs in the capture phase, before the list's own handling.

members.name: filterRows
members.description:
Works out which options the search hides, and hides them with a rule in the select's own shadow root, by position:
the options are the author's light DOM, and nothing is written on them. While there is search text, a heading with
no visible option left in its group hides, and so does every divider.

members.name: handleOverlayBeforeToggle
members.description:
Runs before the dropdown hides, while its rows can still hold focus. A row is light DOM slotted into the popover,
so the browser does not count it as inside the popover and does not hand focus back to the trigger: hiding the
focused row would drop focus to the body. Focus moves back to the trigger here instead. Focus that already left
(Tab, a click elsewhere) is not taken back.

members.name: spacePressedInList
members.description: Whether the last key pressed in the list was Space, which is what arms the keyup guard above.

members.name: pointerOnTrigger
members.description: Set while a pointer is down on the trigger: that click toggles the dropdown itself, so focusout must not.

members.name: handleOverlayFocusOut
members.description: Closes the dropdown when focus moves from a row to something outside it: Tab and Shift+Tab out of the list.

members.name: activeInTree
members.description: The element with focus in this select's tree: a light-DOM row, or the host itself when focus is on the trigger.

members.name: focusIsOnOption
members.description: Focus is on a row or a footer control (light DOM), or on the search field or Create row (the dropdown's shadow DOM).

members.name: focusedOption
members.description:
The row holding the list's roving tabindex: the selected one, else the first enabled one. Falls back to picking it
here when the list has not given any row the tabindex yet (rows replaced just before opening).

members.name: triggerLabel
members.description:
The accessible name for the trigger.

The focusable control is a `<button>` inside the shadow root, and neither of the two ways an author
names this element reaches it on its own: `aria-labelledby` on the host points at an id in the light DOM,
which ARIA cannot resolve across the shadow boundary, and a wrapping `<label>` names the host rather than
the button. So the label's *text* is copied onto the button instead.

members.name: syncLabelText
members.description: Reads the text of whatever labels the host: `aria-labelledby` first, then any associated `<label>`.

events.name: input
events.description: Fired with `selection-change`, after `value` is updated. Carries no detail: it exists so the select behaves like the other form controls, which is what `v-model`, `ngModel` and any generic form binding listen for.

events.name: change
events.description: Fired with `input`. A select commits on every pick, so the two always fire together.

events.name: create-option
events.description: Fired when the "Create" row of a `creatable` select is chosen. `detail.label` is the trimmed search text; add the option and set `value`. Does not bubble.

Fired after the user picks an option. `detail.value` is the array of selected values (one entry unless `multiple`), `detail.data` the `data` of each selected row. Does not bubble: several components fire `selection-change`, so a listener belongs on the element itself rather than on an ancestor.
events.name: selection-change

events.description: Fired, with `searchable`, when the search text changes (and with an empty `detail.query` when closing clears it). Cancel it to filter the options yourself: the select then shows every option it holds. Does not bubble.
events.name: search-change

declarations.description:
A field around the browser's own `<select>`, themed like `c2-text-field`: the phone's own picker, the keyboard and
typeahead of the platform, browser autofill where the browser offers it, and no popover code. Use it where the
operating system's picker is the better experience (forms on phones, long country lists) or where a page should
not load `c2-select`'s listbox. It holds a single value; `c2-select` is the one with search, multiple selection
and rich options.

The options are written as `<option>` and `<optgroup>` children, as in a native select, or given as `options`
(JSON in markup, an array from script): `{ value, label?, disabled? }` objects, plain strings, or groups
`{ label, options, disabled? }`. The children win when both are given. They are copied into the select inside the
shadow root (a native select can only show options it contains) and followed as they change; nothing is written on
them. A `<option selected>` child gives the starting value when the host has no `value` attribute.

`placeholder` adds a first, empty option shown in the placeholder colour while nothing is chosen; with `required`
it cannot be picked back, and the form is invalid until a real option is chosen. Without a placeholder, a value
that matches no option falls back to the first enabled option, as a native select does. While there are no options
yet, `value` keeps what was set, so options that load later can still select it.

The field turns red after the user has left it invalid (`:user-invalid` on the inner select), while `error` is set
and while an enclosing `c2-form-field` shows an error. The host exposes `:state(disabled)`, `:state(error)` and
`:state(empty)` (the placeholder shows).
